prompt: How do I get tree sap off my car in Washington?

answer:
Gemini said

Removing tree sap from your car can be tricky because sap hardens quickly, especially in changing weather, but it is completely manageable with the right household items.

Here are the best, safest methods to get tree sap off your car’s paint and glass in Washington (where sticky sap from evergreens like pine, fir, and cedar is a common headache):

Method 1: Rubbing Alcohol (Best for Fresh or Cured Sap)

Isopropyl (rubbing) alcohol is one of the safest and most effective solvents for breaking down tree sap without damaging your car's clear coat.

Soak a cotton ball or microfiber cloth in 70% or 90% rubbing alcohol.

Press it firmly against the sap spot and hold it there for 30 to 60 seconds to let the alcohol dissolve the sticky resins.

Wipe gently. Avoid scrubbing harshly, which can scratch the paint. If the sap is stubborn, hold the soaked cloth on it a little longer.

Wash the area with mild car soap and water afterward, then apply a quick coat of wax to protect the paint.

Method 2: Bug and Tar Remover or WD-40 (Best for Tough Spots)

If rubbing alcohol isn't cutting it, specialized automotive products or household lubricants work wonders.

Automotive Bug & Tar Remover: Available at any auto parts store (like AutoZone, O'Reilly, or Advance Auto Parts) or major retailer (Walmart). Spray it on, let it sit for a minute or two according to the product instructions, and wipe it away with a microfiber towel.

WD-40: Spray a small amount directly onto the sap, let it sit for about a minute to loosen the bond, and gently wipe it away.

Note: Both of these will strip away any existing wax on that specific spot, so make sure to re-wax the area once you are done.

Method 3: Hand Sanitizer (A Handy Backup)

If you don't have rubbing alcohol on hand, gel hand sanitizer can work in a pinch because of its high alcohol content.

Dab a generous amount of hand sanitizer directly onto the sap spot.

Let it sit for 1 to 2 minutes so the gel stays in contact with the sap.

Wipe away with a microfiber cloth and rinse the area with water.

⚠️ What to Avoid

Do NOT use fingernails, razor blades, or abrasive scrub sponges (like Scotch-Brite pads). These will permanently scratch and ruin your car’s clear coat.

Avoid harsh household cleaners like dish soap, acetone (nail polish remover), or gasoline, as they can strip or dull the paint finish.

Pro-Tip for Washington Drivers

Washington’s damp climate and abundant evergreens mean sap can bake in the sun or get reactivated by rain. Try to remove sap as soon as you notice it—once it bakes in direct sunlight for weeks, it becomes much harder to remove and can actually etch into your clear coat.
